note.label: The Kingdom Of Adam And The Old World

precepts.why:
“The Lord hardened Pharaoh, that he should not know him, that his powerful works might be known to the world.” Read on: “His mercy is manifest to every creature; and he hath separated his light from the darkness with an adamant.” The light stands for good and the darkness for evil, and he separates them with an adamant.

The annotation in the King James gives the meaning of adamant: refusing to be persuaded, or to change one's mind. That is what the hardening of Pharaoh was. God made Pharaoh not be persuaded to let us go. That is the adamant, and that is how God separates his light from the darkness: he hardens a heart so that it will not believe and will not follow. The same way he hardened Pharaoh's heart, he will harden hearts so that people do not believe these scriptures.

So in the beginning, when God separated the light from the darkness, spirits were created, and God said: you I will choose, you are my chosen people; you I will not choose, I will harden your heart. The children of light were chosen, and the darkness was left hardened.

precepts.text: One just child is better than a thousand ungodly; replenish the earth with righteous seed.
precepts.point: Noah and his sons were told to replenish the earth after the flood, and the earth is replenished with righteous children; a multitude of ungodly children profits nothing.

note.label: Genesis 9: The Laws Before Moses and the Covenant of the Bow

precepts.why:
Noah and his sons were told to “Be fruitful, and multiply, and replenish the earth” after the flood. But the earth is replenished with righteous children. “Desire not a multitude of unprofitable children, neither delight in ungodly sons. Though they multiply, rejoice not in them, except the fear of the Lord be with them.”

A multitude of ungodly children profits nothing: “one that is just is better than a thousand; and better it is to die without children, than to have them that are ungodly.” Replenish the earth with righteous seed.

precepts.text: Desire not a multitude of unprofitable children: it is better to have none at all, and to die without children, than to have them that are ungodly and not be able to restrain them from doing evil.
precepts.point: Do not let that be you. Do not let the Lord pass a judgment on your house where Christ prays for you and the Most High says, No, I will bring a judgment on his house for ever. Do not sin a sin so great that it cannot be prayed for, so that nothing is left but the fiery day of judgment.

note.label: 1 Samuel 3: The Lord Reveals Himself to Samuel

precepts.why:
“Desire not a multitude of unprofitable children, neither delight in ungodly sons. Though they multiply, rejoice not in them, except the fear of the Lord be with them.” “for one that is just is better than a thousand; and better it is to die without children, than to have them that are ungodly.” It is better to have none at all than to have them that are ungodly and not be able to restrain them from doing evil.

That was Eli. The Lord said, “I will judge his house for ever for the iniquity which he knoweth; because his sons made themselves vile, and he restrained them not.” Eli let his children break the commandments of the Lord and lead the people astray, and he restrained them not.

So the Lord swore that “the iniquity of Eli’s house shall not be purged with sacrifice nor offering for ever.” When the Lord is mad, the Lord is mad: thus we are in the lands of our captivity 400 years and counting, and you have heard the history of the Spanish Inquisition, how we were burned for keeping the commandments. His anger burns unto the lowest hell.

Do not let that be you. Do not let the Lord pass a judgment on your house where Christ prays for you and the Most High says, No, I will bring a judgment on his house for ever. Do not sin a sin so great that it cannot be prayed for, so that nothing is left but the fiery day of judgment.

points: Desire not a multitude of unprofitable children, neither delight in ungodly sons. Now there is another scripture in Psalms that says it is a good thing to have a lot of kids. But it says here, do not desire a multitude — what is the key word? Unprofitable. Meaning these are wicked kids.

note.label: When Children Walk in a Land of Shadows (Part 2)

points: Trust not thou in their life, neither respect their multitude: for one that is just is better than a thousand; and better it is to die without children, than to have them that are ungodly. It is better to have one good child than a thousand wicked ones. It is better to have no kids at all than to have them that are ungodly.

note.label: When Children Walk in a Land of Shadows (Part 2)

points: Desire not a multitude of unprofitable children, neither delight in ungodly sons. See that? Do not delight in unprofitable children. You know that boy, all them boys, you got them girls, you know if they good or not. If they are unprofitable, do not rejoice in them.

note.label: When Children Walk in a Land of Shadows

points: Though they multiply, rejoice not in them, except the fear of the Lord be with them. That is the only time to rejoice in a bunch of kids. If you have a lot of children, if they fear the Lord, then rejoice. If they do not fear God, do not rejoice.

note.label: When Children Walk in a Land of Shadows

points: Trust not thou in their life. And do not trust in their life. Neither respect their multitude — their numbers.
For one that is just — one just child, one child that keeps the commandments — is better than a thousand. Is better than a thousand unprofitable kids.

And better it is to die without children. It is better to die without ever having children than to have them that are ungodly. Than to have a bunch of ungodly kids. Why? Because they are going to bring shame to you. They will bring shame to you. You will be all on the news.

note.label: When Children Walk in a Land of Shadows

points: The Lord neither spared the place where Lot sojourned but abhorred them for their pride: they worshiped their booty more than God, and today it is happy pride and a flag sent to the sky, spiritual Sodom and Gomorrah back.
He pitied not the people of perdition: the son of perdition, the man of sin, the vessels of wrath; they hide their history, so we reveal it, because their true history is sin.

Who can declare the works of his justice? or who can endure them? A lot of you say you want justice, but you do not understand what God's justice is. You think because the murderers of the past died, that was it for them? God is bringing them back from the dead to judge them; that is Daniel 12. The covenant is afar off, and the trial of all things is in the end. In the end God is judging everybody for what they have done on this earth.

note.label: Seeking Justice in an Unjust System

points: In the congregation of the ungodly shall a fire be kindled; and in a rebellious nation wrath is set on fire. In the beginning, when there was a congregation of the ungodly, he drowned them.

note.label: The Pride Of Thine Heart Hath Deceived Thee!

points: He was not pacified toward the old giants, who fell away in the strength of their foolishness: they were giants, but they were foolish, and people feel strong in their foolishness. Neither spared he the place where Lot sojourned, but abhorred them for their pride.

note.label: The Pride Of Thine Heart Hath Deceived Thee!

points: He pitied not the people of perdition, nor the six hundred thousand footmen, who were gathered together in the hardness of their hearts. How long are you going to keep using somebody's rough life story to excuse the one who refuses correction? If they will not listen to the scripture, stop making excuses for them.

note.label: The Pride Of Thine Heart Hath Deceived Thee!

points: And if there be one stiffnecked among the people, it is marvel if he escape unpunished: one stiffnecked person in the congregation, and it would be a marvel if God lets it go. For mercy and wrath are with him: he is mighty to forgive, and to pour out displeasure. That is why the saying God is good all the time is not scriptural: the same God drowned the whole earth, swallowed rebels alive, and left a generation in the wilderness for forty years. God is good all the time to the people that keep his commandments.
